## Guidance

Not stated as numeric guidance. Outlook paragraph (verbatim):
- "However, the adverse implications of the extended disruption in supply chains and elevated energy prices could interrupt the growth momentum. Inflation is expected to trend higher from its relatively benign levels, driven by higher food, energy prices, weather-related uncertainties, and currency depreciation."
- "...the Company remains committed to delivering sustainable shareholder value by leveraging sector specific technology, investing in AI, and adopt digital solutions to enhance productivity and competitiveness."
- "The Company is also focused on ensuring efficient and profitable execution of its robust order book, maintaining financial discipline, and allocating capital judiciously across targeted growth sectors."

## Management Commentary — Demand

- "Sustaining momentum amid volatility" (Annexure I headline).
- CMD (S N Subrahmanyan): "The financial year has commenced against the backdrop of geopolitical uncertainties. The Company has managed to maintain momentum by rotating its focus across sectors and geographies while maintaining robust cash flows."
- "...we remain confident of maintaining growth while capitalising on emerging opportunities."
- Infrastructure & Utilities: "...receipt of orders for Residential & Commercial buildings and Ferrous Metal projects."
- Energy – Conventional: "The decline reflects the deferment of certain anticipated orders and the high base effect arising from an ultra-mega order secured in the CarbonLite Solutions business in the corresponding period of the previous year."

## Management Commentary — Margins

- Infrastructure & Utilities: "The contraction in margin is primarily on account of change in revenue mix and an increase in credit provisions on account of expected delays in collection of receivables."
- Manufacturing & Products: "The margin is reflective of change in the sales mix within the portfolio."
- Technology, Platforms & Services: "The marginal decline is reflective of higher manpower cost and forex variation adversely impacting hedged portfolio positions."
- Realty: "The decline in margin is primarily due to the change in sales composition."

## Management Commentary — Capacity / Expansion

- Portfolio realignment under Lakshya 2031 (effective 1 April 2026): "Effective from April 01, 2026, pursuant to the Company’s Lakshya 2031 strategic plan, the Group has realigned its portfolio to enhance strategic focus, capital allocation efficiency and operational agility."
- Segment changes: Renewables and Offshore Wind carved out into new "Energy – Green" segment; Realty reported separately.
- Merger (see Named Catalysts): Scheme of Amalgamation of L&T Power Development Limited into the Company.

## Named Catalysts

- Divestment of Nabha Power completed 25 June 2026 (CMD: "During the quarter, we successfully concluded the sale of Nabha Power Limited").
- Hyderabad Metro: "we have signed the share purchase agreement with Hyderabad Metro Rail Limited (“HMRL”), a Government of Telangana Enterprise, to divest 100% of our stake in Hyderabad Metro SPV."
- Scheme of Amalgamation of L&T Power Development Limited (wholly owned subsidiary, unlisted, Transferor Company) with the Company (Transferee) under Sections 230-232 of the Companies Act, 2013, subject to NCLT Mumbai sanction. Networth as on 31 March 2026 (standalone): L&T ₹ 74,532.90 crore; LTPDL ₹ 2,703.12 crore. Per filing: "There will be no change in shareholding pattern of the Transferee Company pursuant to the proposed Scheme."

## Named Risks

- "...the adverse implications of the extended disruption in supply chains and elevated energy prices could interrupt the growth momentum."
- "The resurgence of geopolitical tensions in West Asia and continued uncertainty around global trade policies remains key risks."
- Energy – Green: "...largely due to supply chain disruptions arising from the West Asia conflict in the Solar business."
- Infrastructure & Utilities: "The subdued performance is largely attributed to execution challenges in the Water & Effluent Treatment business."
- Credit: "...an increase in credit provisions on account of expected delays in collection of receivables."
